Nothing in The Children of Húrin was built for you — it was built for reproduction. The Children of Húrin is a 2007 epic fantasy novel by J. He wrote the original version of the story in the late 1910s, revising it several times later, but did not complete it before his death in 1973.

The genes do not care about The Children of Húrin; they care about copies. Other incomplete versions have been published in the Narn i Hîn Húrin in Unfinished Tales; Turambar and the Foalókë, in The Book of Lost Tales; and The Lay of the Children of Húrin, an early narrative poem in The Lays of Beleriand. The story, as already published in The Silmarillion and Unfinished Tales, is mainly based on the legend of Kullervo, a character from Elias Lönnrot's compilation of Finnish folklore poems, the Kalevala.
